classPractice.note: 考点：动词 access 直接接宾语；形容词 accessible 与 be...to sb 搭配。

original_sentence: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips.
readingExamples: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the degree or scale to which something happens or is the case
(2) n. the size, length, or area covered by something; its physical range
(3) n. the limit or point up to which something reaches or applies

posExamples.sentence: Only when the smoke had cleared did the villagers grasp the full extent of the fire's destruction, and a heavy silence settled over the blackened fields. （读后续写·灾后·震惊）
I would like to draw the committee's attention to the extent of the plastic pollution along our riverbank, which has grown far more serious than most residents realise. （应用文·投诉/建议信）
To a large extent, a nation's future is shaped less by its natural resources than by the character and diligence of its young people. （议论文·青年与国家）
As the plane climbed above the clouds, the sheer extent of the mountain range unfolded beneath us, ridge after snow-capped ridge stretching to the very edge of sight. （读后续写·壮景·敬畏）

wordForms.noun: extent (程度/范围); extension (延伸，扩展，延期)
wordForms.other: 词族速记：extend(v.延伸)→extent(n.程度/范围)→extension(n.延伸/延期)→extensive(adj.广泛的)→extensively(adv.)。固定搭配全家桶：to a certain/some/large/great extent、to what extent、to the extent that、to such an extent that；extent 前几乎总用介词 to。

collocations.phrase: to a certain / an / some / a large extent
collocations.translation: 【课件】在一定 / 某种 / 很大程度上
collocations.example: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips. 在一定程度上，世界的知识都触手可及。

collocations.phrase: sb does sth to such an extent that ...
collocations.translation: 【课件】某人做某事到如此程度以致……
collocations.example: He devoted himself to the experiment to such an extent that he forgot to eat and sleep. 他埋头实验，以致废寝忘食。

collocations.translation: 在一定程度上（课文原句：To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips.）
collocations.example: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips. （课文原句）
To some extent, failure teaches us more than easy success ever can. 在某种程度上，失败比轻易的成功教会我们更多。

collocations.translation: 到什么程度，在多大程度上（引导设问或宾语从句）
collocations.example: To what extent do smartphones shape the way we think? 手机在多大程度上塑造了我们的思维方式？
To a large extent, our habits decide who we become. 在很大程度上，习惯决定我们成为怎样的人。
To some extent, failure taught me more than any of my easy victories ever had. （读后续写·成长感悟）
Not until years later did she understand the full extent of the sacrifices her parents had quietly made for her. （读后续写·迟来的领悟）
He devoted himself to the experiment to the extent that he forgot to eat, sleep, or even glance at the clock. （读后续写·忘我·执着）
The drought worsened to such an extent that the once-mighty river dwindled to a thin ribbon of mud. （读后续写·环境·干旱）

collocations.phrase: the extent of the damage / problem
collocations.example: Rescue teams worked through the night to assess the extent of the damage before the second storm arrived. （应用文·新闻报道）
Kindness, stretched beyond a certain extent, can become a burden if it robs others of the chance to stand on their own. （议论文·辩证）

synonyms.example: To a surprising degree, the shy newcomer had won the whole class over within a single week. （读后续写·融入·转变）
synonyms.usage: 与 extent 在'程度'义上高度重合，常可互换(to some degree = to some extent)；degree 略偏'量级、等级'，extent 略偏'范围、幅度'；两者都接 to ... degree/extent

synonyms.example: The scale of the volunteers' effort astonished even the mayor, who had never seen the town so united. （应用文·活动报道）
synonyms.usage: 强调'规模大小'，多用于事件、行动、灾难的体量（on a large scale）；extent 更强调'延伸到哪、覆盖多广'，也可指抽象程度

synonyms.example: Few at the time grasped the magnitude of the discovery, which would one day transform the whole of medicine. （议论文·科学史）
synonyms.usage: 书面且庄重，强调'巨大的规模或重要性'，常带震撼意味；extent 更中性，可大可小，搭配更灵活

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·to such an extent that 引导结果状语从句（课件同款）
advancedExpressions.expression: sb does sth to such an extent that + 结果（相当于 so ... that）
advancedExpressions.example: 课件句型:sb does sth to such an extent that ...。The noise grew to such an extent that no one in the hall could hear the speaker. 噪音大到会场里没人听得见发言者。相当于 so ... that 的程度—结果句。

advancedExpressions.expression: to a certain / some / large / great extent；to what extent；to the extent that
advancedExpressions.example: To a large extent, the harvest depends on the weather; to what extent effort can overcome bad luck, no one can say. （一句内连用多个 extent 结构，展示程度表达梯度）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·在一定程度上
advancedExpressions.expression: to a certain extent = to some degree = in part = up to a point
advancedExpressions.example: To a certain extent (= to some degree = in part) this is true, but it overlooks one crucial fact. （四种可替换的让步表达，写作换用避免重复）

advancedExpressions.expression: to such an extent that + 结果 / to the extent that + 结果
advancedExpressions.example: The noise grew to such an extent that no one in the hall could hear the speaker. （to such an extent that 引导结果状语从句，相当于 so ... that）

advancedExpressions.expression: not until ... did sb. realize the full extent of ...
advancedExpressions.example: Not until she stood alone in the empty house did she realize the full extent of how much a single voice, now silent, had once filled her days. （not until 倒装 + the full extent of，续写高潮处顿悟）

advancedExpressions.expression: to a large extent, ... depends on ...
advancedExpressions.example: To a large extent, the success of this campus recycling drive depends on whether each of us is willing to change one small daily habit. （to a large extent 引出因果，倡议信增强分寸感）

advancedExpressions.expression: to what extent can / should ...?
advancedExpressions.example: To what extent should individual freedom yield to the common good? This is a question every thoughtful citizen must one day confront. （to what extent 设问句破题，引出思辨）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She finally understood how much her parents loved her.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Only when she became a parent herself did she at last grasp the full extent of the love that had once, silently and without complaint, sheltered her from every storm. （读后续写·代际·迟悟）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Only when...did 倒装强调 + grasp the full extent of 名词化提升 + silently and without complaint 副词插入渲染 + sheltered from every storm 隐喻

sentenceUpgrade.original: The problem is very serious.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The extent of the problem has grown to such an alarming degree that we can no longer afford the comfortable luxury of looking the other way. （议论文·警示句）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: the extent of 主语名词化 + to such an alarming degree that 结果状语从句 + can no longer afford 情态否定强化紧迫 + the comfortable luxury of 反讽名词短语

classPractice.question: 在很大程度上，一个人的成功取决于他的坚持。____ ____ ____ ____, one's success depends on his perseverance. （extent）
classPractice.note: 考点：to a large extent 固定短语'在很大程度上'，用 to，不用 in/on。

classPractice.question: The scandal shocked the public to such an ____ (extend) that the minister was forced to resign.
classPractice.note: 考点：to such an ____ that 结构中用名词 extent（相当于 so...that）；注意与动词 extend、名词 extension 区分。

classPractice.question: 选词填空（extent / degree / scale）：Rescue teams still cannot assess the full ____________ of the damage caused by the flood.
classPractice.note: 考点：the full extent of sth 固定搭配，指损害的'全部范围/程度'；此处 scale 也可但 extent 最贴合 the full ... of。

original_sentence: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips.
readingExamples: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. partly but not completely; in some degree though not entirely
(2) phr. used to show that a statement is true up to a point, while acknowledging limits or exceptions

posExamples.sentence: To a certain extent, the long weeks of loneliness had toughened him, teaching the once-pampered boy to cook, to mend, and above all to rely on no one but himself. （读后续写·独立·蜕变）
To a certain extent, I agree that homework helps consolidate what we learn; however, an endless pile of it may do more harm than good to a tired young mind. （应用文·观点信）
To a certain extent, wealth can buy comfort and convenience, yet it can never purchase the quiet contentment that springs from meaningful work and genuine friendship. （议论文·金钱观）
The apology soothed her anger, to a certain extent, but the memory of that cruel remark still lingered like a splinter she could not quite remove. （读后续写·和解·心结未消）

wordForms.other: 结构拆解：to（介词）+ a certain（一定的）+ extent（程度，名词）。可替换核心词：a certain → some / a large / a great；整组常置于句首作让步状语，后接 but/yet/however 转折。近义组：to some degree / in part / up to a point / partly。

collocations.phrase: To a certain extent, ... (= to an / some / a large extent)
collocations.translation: 【课件】在一定程度上（可替换 to an/some/a large extent）
collocations.example: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips. 在一定程度上，世界的知识都触手可及。

collocations.translation: 在一定程度上，……（课文原句：To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips.）
collocations.example: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips. （课文原句）

collocations.translation: 在一定程度上……，但……（先让步后转折的经典写作句式）
collocations.example: To a certain extent, talent matters, but effort matters far more. 在一定程度上天赋很重要，但努力更重要。
I agree to a certain extent with those who praise online learning, though I still cherish the warmth of a real classroom. （议论文·辩证表态）

collocations.phrase: be true to a certain extent
collocations.example: The old saying that practice makes perfect is true to a certain extent, but without reflection, mere repetition leads nowhere. （议论文·反驳俗见）

collocations.phrase: help / affect sb to a certain extent
collocations.translation: 在一定程度上帮助／影响某人
collocations.example: Her encouraging words helped me to a certain extent, yet the courage to go on had to come, in the end, from within. （读后续写·自我觉醒）

collocations.phrase: control / limit sth to a certain extent
collocations.translation: 在一定程度上控制／限制某事
collocations.example: Strict rules can control careless behaviour to a certain extent, but true discipline is born of understanding, not fear. （议论文·教育方式）

synonyms.example: To some degree, the hardship of that winter had prepared me for every trial that came afterwards. （读后续写·磨难·成长）
synonyms.usage: 与 to a certain extent 几乎完全同义，可自由互换；degree 略偏'量级'，两者在写作中交替使用可避免重复，都置于句首或句末

synonyms.example: The victory was, in part, a matter of luck, but mostly the reward of months of quiet, stubborn preparation. （议论文·成败归因）
synonyms.usage: 较简洁书面，强调'部分原因/部分程度'，常与 mostly/largely 对举；语气比 to a certain extent 更干脆，可作插入语

synonyms.translation: 在一定限度内，到某种程度为止
synonyms.example: You may bend the rules up to a point, the old coach warned, but cross that line and you betray the very game you love. （读后续写·师训·底线）
synonyms.usage: 口语化，强调'到某个限度为止、再往前就不成立'，暗含转折与临界感，比 to a certain extent 更突出'界限'

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·让步'在一定程度上'（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: to a certain extent = to some degree = in part = partly = up to a point
advancedExpressions.example: To a certain extent (= up to a point) I share this view, but I cannot accept its extreme conclusion. （五种可替换让步表达，写作换用避免重复）

advancedExpressions.expression: To a certain extent, + 让步观点, but / yet / however + 真正主张
advancedExpressions.example: To a certain extent, competition drives progress, but cooperation nurtures something even more precious. （前半退一步承认，后半 but 亮出真正立场，议论文显分寸）

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., to a certain extent, but ... still ...
advancedExpressions.example: Time had healed the wound, to a certain extent, but on quiet nights the old ache would still steal back, uninvited and undimmed. （to a certain extent 插入分句制造心理层次，续写细腻情感）

advancedExpressions.expression: to a certain extent I share this view, yet ...
advancedExpressions.example: To a certain extent I share the view that competition drives progress, yet I firmly believe cooperation nurtures something even more precious. （委婉赞同后转折，观点信显分寸）

advancedExpressions.expression: to a certain extent ... holds true, but it overlooks ...
advancedExpressions.example: To a certain extent, the argument that money brings happiness holds true, but it overlooks the deeper joys that no fortune can ever buy. （先让步承认合理，再指出局限，思辨严谨）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Her words made me feel a little better.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Her gentle words eased my sorrow, to a certain extent, though the ache of the empty chair at the dinner table was something no comfort could wholly reach. （读后续写·安慰·未愈之痛）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: to a certain extent 插入分句制造情感层次 + the empty chair 具象化意象 + no comfort could wholly reach 否定强化未愈之痛

sentenceUpgrade.original: I partly agree that exams are useful.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: To a certain extent, I concede that examinations serve as a fair measure of diligence; nevertheless, they can never fully capture the creativity and courage that define a truly remarkable mind. （议论文·让步论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: To a certain extent 开篇让步 + concede 正式认同动词 + serve as a measure 名词化搭配 + nevertheless 强转折 + capture creativity and courage 名词并列升华

classPractice.question: 在一定程度上我同意你的看法，但我认为运动同样重要。（用 to a certain extent 开头）
classPractice.answer: To a certain extent, I agree with you, but I think exercise is equally important. / To a certain extent I share your view, yet I believe exercise matters just as much.
classPractice.note: 考点：to a certain extent 作让步状语置于句首，后接 but/yet 引出真正主张。

classPractice.question: To some degree, his rudeness came from shyness rather than pride. → 用 extent 改写：____ ____ ____ ____, his rudeness came from shyness rather than pride.
classPractice.note: 考点：to some degree 与 to a certain extent 同义可互换，均表'在一定程度上'。

translation: 掌握（信息），熟悉、精通（知识等），了如指掌
original_sentence: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips.
readingExamples: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. (of information, facts, or knowledge) readily available and easy to obtain or recall
(2) phr. mastered so thoroughly that one can use or produce it instantly and with ease
(3) phr. within easy reach; conveniently at hand

posExamples.sentence: Years of relentless practice had put every scale and sonata at her fingertips, so that when the spotlight found her, her hands moved as if guided by memory alone. （读后续写·音乐·厚积薄发）
With our new mobile library app, the wisdom of thousands of books will be right at your fingertips, wherever you happen to be. （应用文·产品／活动推介）
In an age when boundless information lies at our fingertips, the true challenge is no longer finding knowledge but learning to sift the valuable from the trivial. （议论文·信息时代）
The old shopkeeper had every price, every customer's name, and every family story at his fingertips, and to step into his little store was to be welcomed like an old friend. （读后续写·人物·温情小店）

wordForms.other: 结构：at + one's（物主代词 my/your/his/our...）+ fingertips（指尖，恒用复数）。两义：①（信息/知识）唾手可得；②（技能/内容）烂熟于心、随时能用。物主代词须随主语变化（at my/your/his fingertips）。别与手部习语 have sb wrapped around one's little finger（把某人玩弄于股掌）混用。

idioms.translation: 对某事了如指掌，随时能用
idioms.example: By the eve of the contest, she had the entire history of the dynasty at her fingertips, ready to answer whatever the judges might throw at her. （读后续写·备赛·胸有成竹）

idioms.idiom: have sb wrapped around one's little finger
idioms.translation: 把某人玩弄于股掌之间（近义手部习语，勿混用）
idioms.example: The clever child soon had her doting grandfather wrapped around her little finger, and he could deny her nothing. （读后续写·祖孙·娇宠）

collocations.translation: 【课件】使……触手可及／唾手可得（课件例：Computer technology puts all the information in the world at our fingertips. 计算机技术使世界上所有的信息都触手可及）
collocations.example: Computer technology puts all the information in the world at our fingertips. （课件原句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】掌握，对……了如指掌；触手可及
collocations.example: Computer technology puts all the information in the world at our fingertips. 计算机技术使世界上所有的信息都触手可及。

collocations.translation: 全都唾手可得／了如指掌（课文原句：the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips 世界的知识都触手可及）
collocations.example: To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is all at our fingertips. （课文原句）

collocations.translation: 对某事了如指掌，随时能调用
collocations.example: A good guide has the town's whole history at her fingertips. 好导游对全城历史了如指掌。
Thanks to the Internet, students today have more information at their fingertips than entire libraries once held. （议论文·科技与学习）

collocations.phrase: have the facts at one's fingertips
collocations.example: A good debater must have the facts at her fingertips, for a single hesitation can hand the advantage to the other side. （议论文·辩论技巧）
Everything you need for a healthy start to the morning is right there at your fingertips in our newly opened campus canteen. （应用文·通知／推介）
To a certain extent, the world's knowledge is now at our fingertips, yet wisdom, unlike information, can never simply be downloaded. （议论文·信息与智慧）

collocations.phrase: put / place sth at sb's fingertips
collocations.example: The new self-service kiosks place a wealth of travel advice at every visitor's fingertips. （应用文·服务介绍）
With a single swipe, a doctor's guidance is now literally at the fingertips of villagers who once had to walk for days to reach a clinic. （议论文·科技普惠）

synonyms.example: Keep a torch at hand, the old ranger warned, for these mountain nights fall faster than any city dweller would believe. （读后续写·野外·叮嘱）
synonyms.usage: 指'在近旁、随时可取'，可指实物或时机(help at hand)；at one's fingertips 更强调'熟练掌握、随手能用'，尤指知识技能

synonyms.example: In a well-planned essay, supporting examples should be readily available, drawn from history, literature, and everyday life alike. （议论文·写作方法）

advancedExpressions.expression: have / put / place sth at one's fingertips；lie / rest at one's fingertips

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·触手可及（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: at one's fingertips = within (easy) reach = at hand = readily available
advancedExpressions.example: Information that was once beyond reach is now within easy reach — indeed, right at our fingertips. （三种可替换表达递进，凸显便捷）

advancedExpressions.expression: years of ... had put ... at sb's fingertips

advancedExpressions.expression: with ..., ... will be right at your fingertips

advancedExpressions.expression: when ... lies at our fingertips, the real challenge is ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: She knew the poem very well and recited it easily.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The poem lay so completely at her fingertips that the verses seemed to rise of their own accord, flowing from her lips as naturally as breathing while the whole hall held its breath. （读后续写·背诵·行云流水）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Nowadays we can find information very easily online.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In an era when a universe of information rests at our fingertips, the mark of a truly educated mind is no longer how much one knows, but how wisely one chooses what is worth knowing. （议论文·观点句）

classPractice.question: 【课件】计算机技术使世界上所有的信息都触手可及。（用 at ... fingertips，put ... at）Computer technology ____ all the information in the world ____ ____ ____.

translation: n. 点击，单击；咔哒声 | vi. & vt. 使发出咔哒声；点击，单击
original_sentence: With the click of a mouse or the touch of a button, it is possible to find out almost anything we care to know, from recipes to travel packages, from military affairs to learning resources.
readingExamples: With the click of a mouse or the touch of a button, it is possible to find out almost anything we care to know, from recipes to travel packages, from military affairs to learning resources.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a short, hard sound like that made when you press a switch or a button
(2) n. the act of pressing a button on a computer mouse or on a website
(3) v. to make a short, hard sound, or to make something do this
(4) v. to press a button on a computer mouse or touchpad to make something happen on the screen

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】（事情）豁然开朗，恍然大悟，突然想通（it all clicked / it clicked that ...）
uncommonMeanings.example: When I saw the television report, it all clicked. 我看到电视报道时才恍然大悟。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】咔嗒一声（开关/关掉），发出咔嗒声（click off）
uncommonMeanings.example: He clicked off the radio. 他咔嗒一声关掉了收音机。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (两人)一见如故，情投意合
uncommonMeanings.example: From the very first conversation, the two exchange students simply clicked — finishing each other's sentences and laughing at jokes no one else could follow. （读后续写·友情萌芽·灵魂契合）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (事情)恍然明白，突然想通
uncommonMeanings.example: She stared at the equation for what felt like an eternity, and then, all at once, it clicked — the answer had been hiding in plain sight the whole time. （读后续写·顿悟时刻·豁然开朗）

posExamples.sentence: The key clicked in the rusty lock, and as the heavy door swung open, a wave of stale air and forgotten memories rushed out to greet the trembling boy. （读后续写·探秘场景·悬念渲染）
I would like to remind every member that once you have filled in the form, simply click the 'Submit' button to complete your registration for the charity run. （应用文·通知）
In today's digital age, information that once took days to gather now lies just a click away, and this astonishing convenience has quietly reshaped the way we think and learn. （议论文·科技与生活）
In the dead silence of the abandoned house, the faint click of a light switch made everyone's heart leap into their throats. （读后续写·惊悚氛围·声音描写）

collocations.example: You can check your email with a click of your mouse. （课件原句）
Click the button and your registration will be complete. 点击按钮，报名即完成。

collocations.translation: 【课件】咔嗒一声关掉（收音机/灯等）
collocations.example: He clicked off the radio. 他咔嗒一声关掉了收音机。

collocations.phrase: it all clicked / it clicked that ...

collocations.example: When I saw the television report, it all clicked. 我看到电视报道时才恍然大悟。/ It suddenly clicked that this was fantastically fun. 我突然明白这实在太有意思了。

collocations.phrase: with the click of a mouse

collocations.translation: 咔哒一声到位；(事情)顺理成章

collocations.phrase: at the click of a button
collocations.example: Nowadays a taxi can be summoned to one's doorstep at the click of a button, a convenience unheard of a generation ago. （议论文·科技便利）

synonyms.example: She gently tapped the touch screen, and the ancient painting bloomed into vivid, living colour before her eyes. （读后续写·科技体验）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:tap 侧重手指在触摸屏上的轻触，常用于手机/平板；click 侧重鼠标按键或发出的咔哒声，也可指点击链接

synonyms.example: Just hit 'Enter' and your essay will be submitted to the online contest automatically. （应用文·操作说明）

advancedExpressions.expression: with the click of a mouse；at the click of a button；click on / click through / click into place

advancedExpressions.expression: and then, all at once, everything clicked

advancedExpressions.expression: simply click ... to ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: She clicked the button and the door opened.

sentenceUpgrade.original: You can find information easily online now.

original_sentence: With the click of a mouse or the touch of a button, it is possible to find out almost anything we care to know, from recipes to travel packages, from military affairs to learning resources.

definitionEn:
(1) n. a small, usually round object that is sewn onto clothes and used to fasten them
(2) n. a small part of a machine that you press to make it work
(3) n. a small object that you press on a computer screen or website to make something happen
(4) v. to fasten a piece of clothing with buttons

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 扣上(纽扣)；button up 扣好
uncommonMeanings.example: Her grandmother knelt down and carefully buttoned up the little girl's coat, murmuring that the winter wind was crueller than it looked. （读后续写·祖孙温情·细节动作）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 徽章，胸章(美式，别在衣服上的圆形小饰物)

posExamples.sentence: With one final button left undone, he stood before the mirror, straightened his collar, and drew a deep breath — today was the day everything would change. （读后续写·出场准备·心理蓄势）
In case of emergency, please press the red button beside the exit, and the alarm will alert every member of staff at once. （应用文·安全须知）
Some argue that modern technology has reduced life to the pressing of buttons, yet this convenience, if wielded wisely, can free us to pursue what truly matters. （议论文·科技双刃剑）

wordForms.other: 同形名动：a button（n.）/ to button（v.扣纽扣）。常用短语：press/push a button（按按钮）、do up/undo a button（扣上/解开）、button up（扣好）、sew on a button（缝纽扣）。习语：on the button（分毫不差/准时）、bright as a button（机灵）、push sb's buttons（戳痛处）。

idioms.translation: 故意惹某人，戳某人痛处
idioms.example: He knew exactly how to push her buttons, and with a single careless remark he sent her storming out of the room. （读后续写·人物冲突·情绪爆发）
The rescue team arrived at nine o'clock on the button, just as the trapped hikers had begun to lose all hope. （读后续写·及时救援）
The new pupil was as bright as a button, answering every question before the teacher had even finished asking. （读后续写·人物刻画）

collocations.translation: 一按按钮之间（课文原句：With the click of a mouse or the touch of a button, ...）

His hands shook so badly that he could barely do up the buttons of his uniform on the morning of the parade. （读后续写·紧张时刻）

collocations.translation: 一按按钮之间，轻而易举

synonyms.example: Her fingers danced across the keys, and the empty page slowly filled with the story she had waited years to tell. （读后续写·创作瞬间）

definitionEn:

translation: 公共事务，政治事务；事件，事情
original_sentence: With the click of a mouse or the touch of a button, it is possible to find out almost anything we care to know, from recipes to travel packages, from military affairs to learning resources.
readingExamples: With the click of a mouse or the touch of a button, it is possible to find out almost anything we care to know, from recipes to travel packages, from military affairs to learning resources.
definitionEn:

(2) n. an event or a series of events, especially one that is talked about or causes problems
(3) n. a matter or situation that concerns a particular person and is their own responsibility
(4) n. a secret sexual relationship between two people, usually when one or both are married to someone else

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】（复数 affairs，恒用复数）（军事/外交/经济/世界等）事务；时事（military / foreign / economic / world / current affairs）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 事件，事情（尤指被广泛谈论或引起麻烦的）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Students should pay attention to current affairs.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is high time that students lifted their eyes from textbooks to the wider world of current affairs, for the leaders of tomorrow must first learn to understand the world they are destined to shape. （议论文·青年责任·呼吁）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is high time that + 虚拟过去式 强烈建议 + lifted their eyes from... to... 对照 + for 引导原因 + destined to shape 使命感收尾

classPractice.question: 【课件】Keeping up with current ____ (affair) helps students broaden their horizons far beyond the classroom.
classPractice.note: 考点（课件）：作'时事/事务'讲固定用复数 affairs（current/foreign/military affairs）。

classPractice.question: 【课件】从菜谱到军事，我们几乎可以查到任何想知道的东西。From recipes to ____ ____, we can find out almost anything we care to know.
classPractice.note: 考点（课件）：课文原句词块 military affairs；作'事务'讲 affairs 恒用复数。

classPractice.question: Keeping up with current ____ helps students broaden their horizons far beyond the classroom. (fill with the correct form of 'affair')
classPractice.note: 作'时事/事务'讲固定用复数 current affairs。

classPractice.question: How she spends her own money is her own ____ (affair / event); no one has the right to interfere.
classPractice.note: one's own affair=某人私事；event 指具体活动/大事，不合语境。

translation: 使显示在计算机屏幕上，调出；提出
original_sentence: In the time it takes to find one book in the library, we can use a search engine to bring up millions of results.
readingExamples: In the time it takes to find one book in the library, we can use a search engine to bring up millions of results.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. v. to mention a subject or start to talk about it
(2) phr. v. to make something appear on a computer screen; to display information
(3) phr. v. to look after and educate a child until he or she is grown up; to raise
(4) phr. v. to make someone stop suddenly (bring sb. up short)

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】（电脑）调出，使显示在计算机屏幕上（to make something appear on a computer screen）（课文义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Click this icon to bring up a new menu. 点击这个图标，调出一个新选单。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】提起（某个话题），说起 = mention
uncommonMeanings.example: The manager wanted to bring it up at the meeting as soon as possible. 经理希望尽快在会议上提出这件事。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】养育，抚养 = raise
uncommonMeanings.example: Her parents died when she was a baby and she was brought up by her aunt. 她还是婴儿时父母就去世了，是姑妈把她抚养大的。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】呕吐，吐出 = vomit up
uncommonMeanings.example: The child brought up everything in the morning. 小孩早上把所有吃的东西都吐了。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （电脑）调出，使显示在屏幕上（课文义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Click the icon to bring up the menu. 点击图标调出菜单。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 提出，说起（话题/问题）
uncommonMeanings.example: He brought up an interesting point at the meeting. 他在会上提出了一个有趣的观点。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 抚养，养育(将孩子养大)
uncommonMeanings.example: Widowed young, she brought up four children single-handedly, wearing her exhaustion like a badge of quiet, fierce love. （读后续写·母爱伟大·人物刻画）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 呕吐(把吃下的东西吐出来，英式口语)
uncommonMeanings.example: The seasick sailor leaned over the rail and brought up everything he had eaten, cursing the day he had ever set foot on a ship. （读后续写·航海遭遇·细节）

posExamples.sentence: Just as the tension began to ease, he suddenly brought up the one subject everyone had silently agreed never to mention, and the room fell deathly quiet. （读后续写·矛盾激化·转折）
I would like to bring up an idea at the next meeting: setting aside one afternoon each month for community volunteer work. （应用文·会议提议）
Whenever the topic of failure is brought up, we should remember that every setback carries within it the seed of an equal or greater lesson. （议论文·挫折观）
With a single tap, the search engine brought up millions of results, and the boy sat back, marvelling at how the whole world now fitted inside a glowing screen. （读后续写·科技惊叹）

idioms.idiom: bring sb. up short / with a start
idioms.translation: 使某人猛地停下/大吃一惊
idioms.example: The sudden cry from the darkness brought her up short, and every hair on the back of her neck stood on end. （读后续写·惊悚瞬间）

idioms.idiom: be brought up to do sth
idioms.example: He had been brought up to keep his word, and no temptation on earth could make him break a promise. （读后续写·品格塑造）

collocations.phrase: bring up results / a menu / sth on the screen
collocations.translation: 【课件】（用电脑）调出，使显示在计算机屏幕上（bring up = to make something appear on a computer screen）（课文原句：a search engine to bring up millions of results）
collocations.example: Click this icon to bring up a new menu. 点击这个图标，调出一个新选单。

collocations.phrase: bring up a subject / topic (= mention)
collocations.translation: 【课件】提起（某个话题），提出 = mention
collocations.example: The manager wanted to bring it up at the meeting as soon as possible. 经理希望尽快在会议上提出这件事。
Her parents died when she was a baby and she was brought up by her aunt. 她还是婴儿时父母就去世了，是姑妈把她抚养大的。
The child brought up everything in the morning. 小孩早上把所有吃的东西都吐了。

collocations.translation: 调出/显示大量结果（课文原句：a search engine to bring up millions of results）
collocations.example: A search engine can bring up millions of results in an instant. 搜索引擎瞬间就能调出数百万条结果。
Don't bring up that topic at dinner. 吃饭时别提那个话题。
She brought up three children on her own. 她独自抚养大三个孩子。

collocations.phrase: bring up a subject / topic / question
collocations.example: She hesitated for a long moment before finally daring to bring up the question that had haunted her for years. （读后续写·鼓起勇气）
May I bring up the matter of the overdue library renovation at tomorrow's assembly? （应用文·请示提议）
The well-brought-up young man rose at once to offer the elderly woman his seat. （读后续写·品德细节）
Please don't bring up the past — some wounds are best left to heal in silence. （读后续写·情感克制）

collocations.phrase: bring up a menu / page / file
collocations.example: One click brought up the entire archive, and there, at last, lay the answer she had searched for all night. （读后续写·真相揭晓）
Several parents brought up serious concerns about the new timetable at the meeting. （应用文·家长会记录）

synonyms.translation: 【课件】提及，说起（bring up 作'提起话题'时 = mention）
synonyms.example: The manager wanted to bring it up (= mention it) at the meeting as soon as possible. 经理希望尽快在会议上提出这件事。
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析（课件）：bring up 作'提起某话题'讲时可用 mention 替换；mention 侧重顺带提到，bring up 常指主动挑起讨论。

synonyms.translation: 【课件】提出；抚养（bring up 作'提出/抚养'时 = raise）
synonyms.example: She was brought up (= raised) by her aunt. 她是姑妈抚养大的。/ He brought up (= raised) an objection at the meeting. 他在会上提出了异议。
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析（课件）：bring up 作'提出问题'和'抚养孩子'两义均可用 raise 替换；raise 较正式书面。

synonyms.translation: 【课件】呕吐，吐出（bring up 作'呕吐'时 = vomit up）
synonyms.example: The child brought up (= vomited up) everything in the morning. 小孩早上把吃的全吐了。
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析（课件）：bring up 作'呕吐'讲（英式口语）时 = vomit up；vomit 更正式/医学，bring up 更口语。

synonyms.example: The reporter raised a question so sharp that the official's confident smile froze on his face. （读后续写·尖锐提问）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:raise 较正式书面，'提出问题/异议'和'抚养'两义皆可，议论文常用；bring up 更口语，日常对话中提起话题多用它

synonyms.example: He casually mentioned that he had once climbed Everest, as though it were the most ordinary thing in the world. （读后续写·轻描淡写）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:mention 只是'顺带提到、点一下'，程度轻；bring up 常指'主动挑起某个话题'，带有引出讨论的意味

synonyms.example: The screen displayed a warning message that made the technician's blood run cold. （读后续写·科技惊悚）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:display 侧重'把信息呈现/显示出来'，中性技术用词；bring up 侧重'通过操作把内容调出来'，强调动作过程

advancedExpressions.expression: bring up 抚养/提出/调出 / bring about 导致 / bring in 引进,带来(收入) / bring out 使显现,出版 / bring down 使下降,击落 / bring back 使回忆起,归还
advancedExpressions.example: The Internet has brought about huge changes: type a word and a search engine brings up millions of results. 互联网带来巨变：输入一个词，搜索引擎就调出上百万条结果。

advancedExpressions.expression: bring up = raise = put forward = come up with = bring forward（提出话题/建议/问题时可替换）
advancedExpressions.example: At the meeting she raised / brought up / put forward a bold new plan. 会上她提出了一个大胆的新方案。

advancedExpressions.expression: just as ..., sb. suddenly brought up ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as the laughter was at its warmest, he suddenly brought up her long-lost brother, and the joy drained from her face in an instant. （时间从句制造反差，续写情绪转折）

advancedExpressions.expression: I would like to bring up ... for your consideration
advancedExpressions.example: I would like to bring up a proposal for your kind consideration: that our class organise a monthly visit to the nearby nursing home. （建议/提议句式，礼貌得体）

advancedExpressions.expression: whenever the topic of ... is brought up, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Whenever the topic of artificial intelligence is brought up, opinions split sharply — some hail it as salvation, others dread it as a threat. （被动引入议题+对比双方观点）

sentenceUpgrade.original: His mother brought him up alone.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Left a widow at twenty-five, his mother brought him up alone through years of biting hardship, never once letting him see the tears she shed in the dark. （读后续写·母爱坚韧·反差）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 过去分词 Left a widow 独立主格铺陈背景 + through years of biting hardship 环境刻画 + never once letting him see 反差细节凸显隐忍之爱

sentenceUpgrade.original: He brought up the topic and everyone went quiet.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: No sooner had he brought up the forbidden topic than a heavy silence descended upon the table, and every pair of eyes dropped, as if the very words had frozen the air between them. （读后续写·尴尬冷场·氛围）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: No sooner had... than 倒装强调突发 + heavy silence descended 拟人 + every pair of eyes dropped 群体动作 + as if 虚拟比喻收束张力

classPractice.type: 语境应用·义项判断（课件）
classPractice.question: 【课件】判断 bring up 在各句中的含义：① Click this icon to bring up a new menu. ② The manager wanted to bring it up at the meeting. ③ She was brought up by her aunt. ④ The child brought up everything in the morning.（调出屏幕 / 提起话题=mention / 抚养=raise / 呕吐=vomit up，各配一句）
classPractice.answer: ① 调出，使显示在屏幕上 ② 提起（话题）=mention ③ 抚养=raise ④ 呕吐=vomit up
classPractice.note: 考点（课件）：bring up 四义——①（电脑）调出显示 ②提起话题(=mention) ③抚养(=raise) ④呕吐(=vomit up)。

classPractice.question: 【课件】点击这个图标，调出一个新选单。Click this icon to ____ ____ a new menu.
classPractice.note: 考点（课件）：bring up=使显示在计算机屏幕上，调出（to make sth appear on a computer screen）。

classPractice.question: 只需片刻，搜索引擎就能调出数百万条结果。In no time, a search engine can ____ ____ millions of results.
classPractice.note: 课文原句义'调出信息'；bring up 此处=在屏幕上显示。

classPractice.question: Widowed at thirty, she managed to ____ ____ her two children entirely on her own. (bring up)
classPractice.note: bring up=抚养；宾语较短时可拆开 bring the children up 或 bring up the children。

classPractice.question: 改写：He raised an objection at the meeting. → He ____ ____ an objection at the meeting.
classPractice.note: raise=bring up（提出）；注意过去式 brought。

original_sentence: No wonder the Internet has now become the first place that the majority of people turn to for information.
readingExamples: No wonder the Internet has now become the first place that the majority of people turn to for information.
definitionEn:
(1) n. most of the people or things in a group; more than half of a total number or amount
(2) n. the difference between the number of votes gained by the winning party or candidate and those gained by the next
(3) n. (law) the age at which sb. is legally considered to be an adult and responsible for their own actions

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 大多数，大部分（the majority of + 名词）
uncommonMeanings.example: The majority of the students passed the exam. 大多数学生通过了考试。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 多数票，（选举中的）优势票数
uncommonMeanings.example: She won by a majority of 3,000 votes. 她以三千票的优势获胜。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 成年（法定年龄，通常18岁）
uncommonMeanings.example: On the very day he reached his majority, Tom walked into the lawyer's office, signed the papers with a steady hand, and finally claimed the inheritance his late father had left in trust. （读后续写·成长·继承）

posExamples.sentence: As the votes were counted one by one, a tense silence gripped the hall; when the chairman finally announced that the reform had passed by a slim majority, the room erupted into deafening cheers. （读后续写·投票·紧张氛围）
According to our recent survey, the vast majority of students would welcome a longer lunch break, and I am therefore writing to urge the school to reconsider the current timetable. （应用文·建议信）
Although the majority is not always right, a healthy society must still respect the will of the many while carefully protecting the rights of the few. （议论文·民主与权利）
The government's proposal was approved with an overwhelming majority, giving the new leadership a clear mandate to push through the long-awaited changes. （应用文·新闻报道）

wordForms.noun: majority (n. 大多数) / minority (n. 少数，反义)
wordForms.adjective: major (adj. 主要的) / minor (adj. 次要的，反义)
wordForms.other: 反义词 minority（少数）；主谓一致：the majority of + 复数名词，谓语用复数；the majority 单独作主语、强调整体时可用单数（如 The majority was against the plan.）

collocations.example: The great/vast majority of people seem to agree with the proposal. 似乎绝大多数人都同意这一提案。（课件例句）
People who can speak English in this company are in the majority. 这个公司里会说英语的人占大多数。（课件·完成句子）

collocations.translation: 大多数人（the majority 单独作主语，视整体/个体可用单数或复数）【课件】
collocations.example: The majority was in favour of banning smoking; a small minority were against it. 大多数人支持禁烟，少数人反对。（课件·主谓一致）

collocations.phrase: win by a narrow / large majority
collocations.translation: 以微弱／巨大的多数票获胜【课件】
collocations.example: The Socialists won by a narrow/large majority. 社会党党员获得的票数稍微／远远超出对手，在选举中获胜。（课件例句）

collocations.translation: 大多数人（课文原句：the first place that the majority of people turn to for information）
collocations.example: The majority of people now turn to the Internet first for information. 如今大多数人首先上网找信息。

collocations.phrase: the majority of + 复数名词 + 复数动词
collocations.translation: 大多数……（主谓一致：谓语随of后名词，用复数）
collocations.example: The majority of students prefer online learning. 大多数学生更喜欢在线学习。
The vast majority of volunteers agreed to stay behind, rolling up their sleeves to clean the flooded classrooms long after night had fallen. （读后续写·志愿·奉献）
The motion was carried by a large majority, and the committee immediately set about putting the new recycling scheme into practice. （应用文·会议记录）
The candidate who best listens to ordinary voters is the one most likely to win a decisive majority in the coming election. （议论文·选举）
Because no party secured an absolute majority, the rival groups were forced, however reluctantly, to form a coalition. （应用文·时事评论）
The final plan was adopted by a majority vote, though the headmaster promised that the concerns of the minority would not be ignored. （议论文·集体决策）
Once she reached the age of majority, she was at last free to make her own choices—and to bear their consequences. （读后续写·成长）

synonyms.example: Most of the audience had never seen such a performance, and they rose to their feet, applauding until their palms stung. （读后续写·演出）
synonyms.usage: most 更口语、更常用，后接可数复数或不可数名词；majority 更正式、强调'超过半数'的比例，常用于统计、投票语境

synonyms.example: The bulk of the donations came from ordinary citizens who could ill afford to give, yet gave anyway. （读后续写·慈善）
synonyms.usage: the bulk of 强调'数量或体量上的大部分'，多修饰不可数或整体事物；majority 更侧重'人或可数事物中超过半数'

synonyms.example: The preponderance of scientific evidence points firmly to human activity as the driving force behind climate change. （议论文·环保）
synonyms.usage: preponderance 极正式，多见于学术、法律议论文，强调'压倒性的多数或分量'；majority 通用度更高

advancedExpressions.expression: the majority of + 复数名词 → 谓语用复数；the majority 单独作主语 → 视为整体可用单数、强调个体成员可用复数（The majority was/were）
advancedExpressions.example: The majority of people turn to the Internet.（随of后复数名词，用复数）/ The majority was against the plan.（作整体，单数）/ The majority were in favour.（强调成员，复数）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·majority vs minority（课件对比）
advancedExpressions.expression: the majority 多数(人) ↔ the minority 少数(人)；两词单独作主语时均依整体/个体定单复数；win by a majority 以多数票获胜
advancedExpressions.example: The majority are in favour of the plan; only a minority object. 多数人赞成这个计划，只有少数人反对。The candidate won by a narrow majority. 该候选人以微弱多数票获胜。

advancedExpressions.expression: the majority of = most of = the greater part of = the bulk of（表'大部分'时可替换，majority/most 后接可数复数最常见）
advancedExpressions.example: Most of / The majority of the audience rose to their feet. 大部分观众起立。

advancedExpressions.expression: as the majority ..., a wave of ... swept through ...
advancedExpressions.example: As the majority of the crowd fell silent, a wave of anticipation swept through the stadium, thick enough to touch. （用majority制造集体反应 + a wave of...情绪蔓延，续写高潮铺垫）

advancedExpressions.expression: surveys reveal that the majority of ... , which suggests that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Surveys conducted last month reveal that the majority of residents support the new bike lanes, which strongly suggests that the plan deserves the council's backing. （用调查数据 + which suggests 引出建议，倡议信/建议信标配）

advancedExpressions.expression: while the majority may ..., it does not follow that ...
advancedExpressions.example: While the majority may favour convenience over privacy, it does not follow that we should surrender our personal data without a second thought. （while让步 + it does not follow that逻辑否定，驳论有力）

advancedExpressions.expression: the majority of + 复数名词 → 谓语用复数；the majority 单独作整体主语 → 可用单数
advancedExpressions.example: The majority of people turn to the Internet.（复数）/ The majority was in favour.（作整体，单数）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Most people at the meeting agreed with the plan.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: One after another the hands went up, until it was clear beyond doubt that the plan had the backing of the overwhelming majority—and in that moment, resistance simply melted away. （读后续写·场面描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 动作细节(hands went up)替代抽象'agreed' + beyond doubt强化确定性 + the overwhelming majority升级'most' + 破折号补充画面收束

sentenceUpgrade.original: The majority of students want more sports activities.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is worth noting that the overwhelming majority of students, as our questionnaire clearly indicates, are eager for a richer variety of sporting activities on campus. （应用文·建议信）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is worth noting that正式引出 + as our questionnaire indicates插入语提供依据 + are eager for替代口语want + a richer variety of词汇升级

classPractice.type: 完成句子（课件·语境应用）
classPractice.question: 这个公司大多数人能说英语。The majority of people in this company can speak English. 会说英语的人占大多数。People who can speak English in this company ____ ____ ____ ____ .
classPractice.note: 课件原题；be in the majority=占多数，主语 People 用复数 are。

classPractice.type: 选词填空（课件·多数/少数对比）
classPractice.question: The ____ (majority / minority) are in favour of banning smoking, while only a small ____ (majority / minority) are against it.
classPractice.note: 课件对比点：the majority 多数 ↔ the minority 少数；the majority 单独作主语意为'多数人'。

classPractice.question: The majority of students in our class ____ (spend) more than two hours online every evening.
classPractice.note: the majority of + 复数名词，谓语用复数 spend。

classPractice.question: 互联网已成为大多数人首先求助获取信息的地方。The Internet has become the first place that ____ ____ ____ people turn to for information.
classPractice.note: 课文原句词块 the majority of；后接复数名词。

classPractice.question: Although girls are in the ____ (majority / minority) in this club, boys still speak up most often.
classPractice.note: be in the majority=占多数；minority 为其反义（少数）。

original_sentence: The Internet has also made our lives unbelievably convenient, with all sorts of goods and services provided by electronic commerce, more commonly known as e-commerce.
readingExamples: The Internet has also made our lives unbelievably convenient, with all sorts of goods and services provided by electronic commerce, more commonly known as e-commerce.
definitionEn:
(1) n. (plural) things that are produced to be sold; products or merchandise
(2) n. (British English) things that are transported by road, train, sea or air; freight
(3) n. (law, dated) personal possessions or movable property that a person owns

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 商品，货品（恒为复数，无单数形式；作主语谓语用复数）
uncommonMeanings.example: The goods were delivered on time. 货物按时送到了。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （英）（铁路/公路运输的）货物，货运（a goods train 货运列车）

advancedExpressions.expression: site (地点/网站) / sight (视力,景象,眼前一亮) / cite (引用) —— 三者同音,拼写和词义各异,书写勿混

original_sentence: Gone are the days of searching shop after shop for the perfect pair of boots—you can compare styles and prices quickly and easily in the comfort of your living room.
readingExamples: Gone are the days of searching shop after shop for the perfect pair of boots—you can compare styles and prices quickly and easily in the comfort of your living room.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a strong shoe that covers the foot and the lower part of the leg
(2) n. (British English) the enclosed space at the back of a car where you put luggage; (American English) the trunk
(3) vt. (computing) to start a computer and make it ready to use; to boot up
(4) vt. (informal) to kick something hard

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 靴子（高帮，包住脚踝甚至小腿；课文义）
uncommonMeanings.example: She pulled on her hiking boots and set off. 她穿上登山靴出发了。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （计算机）启动，开机（常用 boot up）
uncommonMeanings.example: She pressed the power button, waited for the ancient laptop to boot up with its familiar groan, and began to type the letter she had put off for far too long. （读后续写·科技·内心挣扎）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （英）汽车后备箱（=美式 trunk）
uncommonMeanings.example: He heaved the last suitcase into the boot, slammed it shut with a satisfying thud, and turned to take one final look at the house he might never see again. （读后续写·离别·出发）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （口语）解雇（give sb. the boot）
uncommonMeanings.example: After years of loyal service, he was given the boot without so much as a word of thanks—a cruelty he would never quite forgive. （读后续写·职场·委屈）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （熟词僻义）而且，另外（to boot，用于句尾，加强语气）
uncommonMeanings.example: He is clever, and hard-working to boot. 他很聪明，而且还很勤奋。

posExamples.sentence: Gone are the days of searching shop after shop for the perfect pair of boots—now, warm and comfortable, you can compare styles and prices in your own living room. （应用文·科技·课文相关）

idioms.idiom: give sb. the boot / get the boot

idioms.idiom: the boot is on the other foot
idioms.translation: 情况反过来了，形势逆转
idioms.example: For years he had mocked his younger brother's dreams; now, watching that same brother succeed, he realized the boot was firmly on the other foot. （读后续写·反转·反思）

idioms.translation: 死在岗位上，奋斗到最后一刻

collocations.translation: 登山靴 / 步行靴 / 雨靴

synonyms.example: She slipped off her muddy shoes at the doorway, unwilling to soil the freshly mopped floor. （读后续写·日常）

synonyms.example: He tossed the spare tyre into the trunk and wiped the grease from his hands on his old jeans. （读后续写·日常）

original_sentence: When you wish to go on holiday, you can make all your travel arrangements just in front of the computer.
readingExamples: When you wish to go on holiday, you can make all your travel arrangements just in front of the computer.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a plan or preparation that you make so that something can happen in the future
(2) n. an agreement between people about how something should be done
(3) n. a group of things placed in a particular position or order, especially in an attractive way
(4) n. a piece of music that has been adapted so that it can be played in a different way from the original

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 改编曲（把乐曲改写成另一种演奏形式）
uncommonMeanings.example: She played her own arrangement of an old folk tune, and the familiar melody, reborn under her fingers, wrapped the silent hall in a warmth no one had expected. （读后续写·音乐会·旧曲新声）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （花草、物品的）布置，摆设
uncommonMeanings.example: On the windowsill stood a modest arrangement of wildflowers she had picked that morning — a small burst of colour that transformed the bare little room into something like home. （读后续写·环境描写·温情细节）

posExamples.sentence: As the departure day drew near, Grandma checked the travel arrangements one last time, her trembling fingers smoothing the tickets as if to make certain this long-dreamed-of journey were truly about to begin. （读后续写·亲情·出发前夜）

I am writing to confirm the arrangements for our upcoming charity book sale: the venue has been booked, volunteers assigned, and posters printed, so that everything may run smoothly on the day itself. （应用文·通知/确认信）

Whatever fine arrangements a school may make for online learning, they can never fully replace the spark of face-to-face discussion, where ideas collide and understanding truly takes root. （议论文·线上学习的局限）

By mutual arrangement, the two neighbours agreed to take turns watering each other's gardens whenever either family was away — a quiet pact that grew, over the years, into a lasting friendship. （读后续写·邻里·约定）

collocations.example: When you wish to go on holiday, you can make all your travel arrangements just in front of the computer. 想度假时，你坐在电脑前就能把旅行都安排妥当。（课件·课文原句）

the arrangement of heavy industry 重工业布局（课件例句）

collocations.translation: 把旅行都安排妥当（课文原句词块）

collocations.phrase: make arrangements (for sth / to do sth)

synonyms.example: Weeks of careful preparation went into the ceremony, and not a single detail was left to chance. （应用文·活动）

original_sentence: Forgot to carry cash? There is no need to worry—you can pay for almost everything on your smartphone.
readingExamples: Forgot to carry cash? There is no need to worry—you can pay for almost everything on your smartphone.
definitionEn:

(2) n. (informal) money in any form
(3) v. to exchange a cheque, traveller's cheque, etc. for coins or notes

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 把（支票等）兑现

In an age when a mere tap of a phone settles any bill, one might ask whether physical cash still has a place in our daily lives — and the answer, for many elderly people, is a resounding yes. （议论文·移动支付与老年群体）

original_sentence: Above all else, the Internet helps us establish and maintain social ties.
readingExamples: Above all else, the Internet helps us establish and maintain social ties.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. more than anything else; used to emphasise that one thing is the most important
(2) phr. (used to introduce the point one considers most significant of all)

posExamples.sentence: She had lost the race, lost the medal, lost even her composure at the finish line — but above all else, she had lost the fear that had chained her for years, and that, she knew, was a victory of its own. （读后续写·成长·内心蜕变）
Our club offers many activities, but above all else, we value the friendships you will build here, for these are the bonds that will outlast any single event. （应用文·社团招新）
A good education should sharpen the mind and broaden the horizon; but above all else, it must teach the young to think for themselves rather than merely to memorise. （议论文·教育本质）
The old fisherman had taught his grandson many things about the sea, but above all else, he had taught him patience — the quiet art of waiting without losing hope. （读后续写·传承·祖孙）

collocations.translation: 最重要的是……（课文原句词块，句首插入语）
collocations.example: Above all else, the Internet helps us establish and maintain social ties. 最重要的是，互联网帮助我们建立并维系社会关系。（课文原句）

collocations.phrase: value / treasure sth above all else
collocations.example: In a world obsessed with success, she treasured honesty above all else. 在痴迷成功的世界里，她把诚实看得高于一切。
The young scientist prized truth above all else, refusing to bend her findings to please anyone. （读后续写·科研·气节）
Above all else, remember that failure is not the opposite of success but a stepping stone toward it. （应用文·赠言/演讲）

synonyms.example: Be brave, be honest, and above all, be true to yourself. （应用文·赠言）
synonyms.usage: 与 above all else 意思几乎相同，用法更常见、更简短；above all else 中的 else 加强了"胜过其余一切"的对比意味，语气更强

synonyms.example: Most importantly, the project taught us how to cooperate under pressure. （议论文·总结）
synonyms.usage: 语气较中性、书面，常作插入语列举要点时的"最后压轴"项；above all else 更有情感重量和文学色彩

synonyms.example: First and foremost, a leader must earn the trust of those he leads. （议论文·领导力）
synonyms.usage: 强调"位居首位"的重要性，语气正式；常置于句首领起论点，与 above all else 可互换但更侧重"顺序上的第一"

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能=表"最重要的是"（句首领起/压轴强调）
advancedExpressions.expression: above all else ≈ above all ≈ most importantly ≈ first and foremost ≈ more than anything (else)
advancedExpressions.example: 都用于突出最关键的一点；above all else 情感/文学色彩最浓，first and foremost 更侧重"顺序上的第一"，most importantly 最中性书面。

advancedExpressions.expression: above all else 中 else 修饰不定代词/all，意为"其他一切"，故 above all else = 胜过其余一切
advancedExpressions.example: 对比 something else 别的东西、anyone else 其他任何人；else 一律后置。

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., but above all else, sb. had learned/gained ...
advancedExpressions.example: The journey had cost her much, but above all else, she had gained something no map could ever chart — faith in herself. （用转折引出最深层的收获，续写结尾点题）

advancedExpressions.expression: above all else, let us remember that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Above all else, let us remember that protecting our environment is not a task for tomorrow but a duty for today. （倡议信结尾拔高，us 拉近距离）

advancedExpressions.expression: ..., and, above all else, ...

sentenceUpgrade.original: The most important thing is that we stayed together.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: We had weathered the storm, salvaged what we could, and comforted one another through the longest of nights; but above all else, we had stayed together — and in that unbroken circle of hands lay a strength no disaster could ever tear apart. （读后续写·团结·主旨升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 三个动作 weathered/salvaged/comforted 铺陈 + but above all else 转折压轴 + in...lay a strength 倒装收束 + "unbroken circle of hands"意象点睛

sentenceUpgrade.original: Honesty is the most important quality.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: A leader may possess intelligence, charisma and vision, yet above all else, it is honesty that wins lasting trust — for people will forgive a mistake far sooner than they forgive a lie. （议论文·品格论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 先列三项优点作让步 + yet above all else 转折突出核心 + it is...that 强调句锁定"honesty" + for 引导原因作论证支撑

translation: 建立（关系或联系）；设立；确立；使得到认可；查实，确定
original_sentence: Above all else, the Internet helps us establish and maintain social ties.
readingExamples: Above all else, the Internet helps us establish and maintain social ties.
definitionEn:
(1) vt. to start or create an organization, a system, a relationship, etc. that is meant to last for a long time
(2) vt. to discover or prove the facts of a situation; to find out something for certain
(3) vt. to make people accept and recognize you or your reputation, especially by your achievements
(4) vt. to make a situation, way of doing things, or belief begin to exist and become accepted

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 确立（地位），使立足；使（信念/传统）获得公认（establish oneself as / get established）【课件】
uncommonMeanings.example: It was the war that established the independence of the United States. 正是这次战争确立了美国的独立。Traditions get established over time. 传统随着时间推移而得到认可。（课件·义项③）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 查实，证实，确定（事实/真相）——高考熟词僻义高频考点
uncommonMeanings.example: The detective would not rest until he had established beyond doubt who had entered the room that fateful night. （读后续写·悬疑·探案）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使确立地位；使得到公认（establish oneself as）
uncommonMeanings.example: Within a single season, the unknown rookie had established herself as the finest player the team had ever seen. （读后续写·励志·崭露头角）

posExamples.sentence: It took years of patient kindness before the shy orphan finally established a bond of trust with the family who had taken him in, but once formed, that bond proved unbreakable. （读后续写·亲情·信任的建立）
To promote reading among students, we propose to establish a book-sharing corner in the classroom where everyone may borrow and lend freely. （应用文·建议信）
Only when a society establishes firm rules that apply equally to all can genuine fairness take root and flourish. （议论文·规则与公平）
After hours of careful investigation, the committee at last established the true cause of the accident, laying to rest weeks of rumour and blame. （读后续写/议论文·查明真相）

wordForms.other: well-established（adj. 根基牢固的）

collocations.example: 1) establish contact/a relationship with sb 与某人建立联系。（课件·义项①建立）

collocations.translation: 创立（一个新的研究中心）＝set up【课件】

collocations.translation: 确立……的地位，使立足【课件】

collocations.translation: 确立声誉，使获得认可【课件】

4) establish the facts/truth 证实事实/真相。（课件·义项④证实）

an establishment = a business organization 企业；the establishment of the club 俱乐部的创立。（课件·n. establishment）

collocations.translation: 建立并维系社会关系（课文原句词块）

collocations.translation: 建立关系 / 联系 / 纽带
collocations.example: The exchange programme helped the two schools establish lasting ties. 交流项目帮两校建立了长久的联系。
The committee finally established that the fire had started in the kitchen. 委员会最终查明火灾始于厨房。

collocations.translation: 一家根基牢固的老牌公司
collocations.example: She left a well-established company to start her own small workshop. 她离开一家老牌公司去创办自己的小作坊。
Through sheer perseverance, she established herself as a voice no one in the debate could afford to ignore. （读后续写·成长）
Thanks to the Internet, we can now establish contact with friends on the far side of the globe in an instant. （议论文·科技拉近距离）
